traceability.notes:
The implementation of Story 007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING is fully present and verified.
All core rules mentioned in the story (`require-story-annotation`, `require-req-annotation`, `require-branch-annotation`, `valid-annotation-format`, `valid-story-reference`, `valid-req-reference`) define specific, actionable error messages in `meta.messages` that follow the shared conventions described in the story: function-related placeholders (`{{name}}` / `{{functionName}}`), branch-related `{{missing}}`, format-related `{{details}}`, and file/reference-related `{{path}}`, `{{storyPath}}`, and `{{reqId}}`.
Tests explicitly tied to docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md validate that: - Missing @story annotations produce a clear message, correct messageId, correctly populated data object (including function name), and ESLint suggestions with a concrete example (REQ-ERROR-SPECIFIC, REQ-ERROR-SUGGESTION, REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT, REQ-ERROR-LOCATION). - Plugin configuration maps severities exactly as specified: format validation (`valid-annotation-format`) as a warning, and all missing-annotation and reference-validation rules as errors (REQ-ERROR-SEVERITY).
The full Jest suite, including tests for error-reporting and configuration severity, passes successfully, confirming that these behaviors are implemented and stable. Based on this concrete evidence, all acceptance criteria and listed requirements in docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md are satisfied.
